A slightly unconventional answer given the game genre, but Terraria is quite a responsive platformer with lots of mechanics, abilities and loot but the basic overworld level design is fairly repetitive despite being procedurally generated. Sure there are differing biomes and enemies but the fundamental level you are walking on is mostly quite basic.

Starbound feels like it recognises this and so it has some content that isn't randomly generated, or is at least more structured, like missions with boss encounters and teleporters to worlds that are platformer tests (lots of spike traps, lava, spinning saws etc).

There's something to be learnt from this, namely that procedurally generated content isn't inherently better than manually made content. It's best when developers respect and use both aspects of design to their full potential.

Most poorly designed Mario ROM hacks. By definition Super Mario Bros 1/3/World/New Super Mario Bros/Super Mario 64/etc have good gameplay mechanics and responsive controls, but the level design in a poorly done mod of those games can be utterly atrocious and make the game painful to play.
